Chiefs have a chance to bury their painful Thanksgiving history in Buffalo

The Chiefs are 5-6 all-time on Thanksgiving, with last year's loss sparking the worst skid of the Mahomes-Reid era. Thursday's matchup in Buffalo offers a chance to exorcise those demons and return to .500 on the holiday.
ByShawn O'Brate|Nov 26, 2026, 9:00 AM EST
Add us as a preferred source
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:51
Instaread

The Kansas City Chiefs have become known for their massive success and their emerging dynasty over the past seven years, but with that success, there has been an enraging plague of bad losses on major holidays. That does not bode well for Kansas City and its matchup in Buffalo on Thursday night while families around the country celebrate Thanksgiving by the television.

Kansas City is 5-6 all-time on Thanksgiving Day, with three of the wins coming at Arrowhead, while five losses have occurred on the road. Again, that does not bode well for Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid this Thursday.

But it's not all bad. Thursday night's game in Buffalo will mark the 20th anniversary of the first-ever Thursday Night Football game, which Kansas City was also a part of, beating Denver 19-10. That marked the Chiefs' second straight victory when playing on Thanksgiving, following a 28-24 win in Detroit ten years prior.

But when looking at the Thanksgiving losses in Kansas City's history, whether it be in 1995 at Dallas (24-12) or the two in Detroit between 1971 and 1981, nothing compares to last season's calamitous loss on "Turkey Day."

Why last Thanksgiving still stings for the Chiefs

Not all losses are created equally, though, especially last season's devastating 31-28 loss at "Jerry World" in Arlington, Texas. That loss, which was strongly affected by Kansas City's 10 penalties for nearly 120 yards, was particularly tough for the Chiefs because it set into motion a six-game losing streak that ended the 2025 season.

If one were to simply look at the box score from last Thanksgiving, they would think Kansas City did not deserve to win anyway. KC had fewer first downs (19) than Dallas (23), fewer rushing yards, and fewer passing yards. Mahomes was sacked thrice, while Dak Prescott was not sacked at all, and Reid's offense only converted 5 of 13 third downs (38.5%).

Still, the Chiefs held a lead for much of the first half and briefly regained the lead in the fourth quarter after a second touchdown by Rashee Rice to start the fourth quarter (below).

After that play, it was the Cowboys who took control, putting up 11 unanswered points and holding on for the victory even after a toe-tapping 10-yard touchdown by Marquise "Hollywood" Brown with a little over three minutes to go.

The loss left a sour taste in the mouths of Mahomes and the rest of the Chiefs, who had put up 28 or more points in a loss for the second time that season—a rarity ever since Steve Spagnuolo joined Kansas City. It would also be the last time that Kansas City would score 14 or more points all season, largely due to Mahomes' season-ending injury two weeks later.

Ever since Thanksgiving last season, the Chiefs have had to be reminded of losing to "America's Team" and how that loss tipped the first domino that would eventually end in the most disastrous season Kansas City has suffered since Reid showed up in 2013. Now is the time to right the wrong, steer the ship back to level, and take down Kansas City's biggest rival of the last six years at the same time.

Kansas City can even its Thanksgiving record with a win

The Chiefs' current record of 5-6 spans all the way back to 1960, when the Chiefs were still the Dallas Texans, losing to the then-New York Titans by a score of 41-35. They then lost their second-ever Thanksgiving game seven years later at home against the Oakland Raiders by a gut-wrenching score of 44-22.

A win on Thursday night would return KC to .500 on Thanksgiving for the first time since that first-ever TNF game 20 years ago. That would also put the Chiefs at .500 on both Thanksgiving and Christmas, as they are 3-3 all-time on Christmas Day, despite losing two of three since 2023.

How Patrick Mahomes has performed on major holidays

Mahomes is known for bringing his best when the lights are brightest, and there are not many lights brighter than Thanksgiving Day prime-time slots. Because of that, it's easy to think that Mahomes will have yet another glorious game on Thursday. Based on history, that wouldn't be too far-fetched.

That's because last year's Thanksgiving Day loss was not on the shoulders of Mahomes, unlike some losses, like last year's Houston game or the Tennessee loss from 2021. Last year, Mahomes put up four passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and completed over 67% of his passes to finish with a passer rating of 129.7. The loss was hardly his fault.

In the other major holiday games of his career (i.e., Christmas Day 2023 and 2024), Mahomes has had two very different games. The Christmas Day disaster against the Raiders in 2023 can easily be seen as partially his fault, especially after a terrible pick-six (below) that immediately followed a scoop-and-score seven seconds earlier.

The other Christmas game that Mahomes played was the polar opposite of his Raiders meltdown, dropping three touchdowns through the air at Pittsburgh back in 2024. He completed over 76% of his passes for 320 yards to finish with a passer rating of 127.1, his highest mark of the season.

So despite his 816 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and one interception over the course of his three major holiday games, he's 1-2. That could also be a record that evens itself out with another historic win over Buffalo, the team that has consistently had Kansas City's number during regular-season matchups.

Only time will tell which Mahomes we get on Thursday night, but history would suggest that if a loss were to end up in the record book, it would not be on the shoulders of No. 15, as he typically plays lights out when the lights are bright.
